subject: Post-demo: hosting criteria + migration scenarios for FinPay
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Cho <acho@finpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: hosting criteria + migration scenarios for FinPay

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Below is a concise recap and a few clarifying questions so we can tailor the follow-up workshop for the right migration path.

What we heard (summary)
- Primary goal: move production chat + AML reranking pipelines to an inference platform with predictable latency (p95 < 250ms) and cost controls.
- Current footprint: mixed — stimulus models on Anthropic via API for prod; research/testing on a legacy on-prem GPU pool that runs custom quantized checkpoints; some near-term E2E throughput spikes during month-end.
- Security/regulatory: need VPC + KMS integration for sensitive PII flows; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Data residency: do the transactions that go through the chat/rerank pipeline require strict US-only hosting?
2) Migration preference: are you aiming to (a) consolidate onto a Hosted API quickly, (b) reserve Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or (c) a Private VPC/on-prem deployment for full control? It’s OK if you need a hybrid (e.g., Hosted for non-sensitive, Private VPC for PII).
3) What does your current SLAs/latency baseline look like on Anthropic for the critical routes? (tokens per minute, avg latency)

Recommended next steps from our side:
- Technical migration workshop: deep dive with your infra + security (2 hrs) to map endpoints, auth, and KV cache migration plan.
- Cost/throughput estimate: we’ll produce a short doc comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for your 6/12-month traffic projections.
- SOC2 + procurement pack: attach the SOC2 stub and our Deploy Matrix for your legal/procurement review.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-matrix.pdf (matrix of tradeoffs), finpay-current-architecture.png (draft we sketched during call)

Thanks — if you can reply with the answers to Q1–Q3 and a couple of time windows next week we’ll lock in the workshop.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
--Attachment: redwood-deploy-matrix.pdf (application/pdf)
--Attachment: finpay-current-architecture.png (image/png)

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the recap and the materials. Quick answers below then a few asks: 

Answers:
- Q1: Yes, transaction data and any PII must remain US-only for now.
- Q2: Desired end state is Private VPC for production (compliance + auditability), but we’re open to a staged approach: Hosted for non-PII and Dedicated for predictable throughput while we move sensitive traffic to VPC.
- Q3: On Anthropic our p95 for short-chat routes is ~180–220ms, monthly tokens ~25M, and peak bursts up to 2.5x baseline during billing cycles.

A few asks for the workshop:
- Can you include a migration sketch for our legacy on-prem pool (we'd like to understand the effort to migrate quantized checkpoints and KV materialization)?
- Security wants the SOC2 evidence and a short list of required network ports for VPC peering. They attached an internal checklist (see attached).

Attaching: "soc2-freestanding.pdf" (internal requester)

Available windows: Tue 9/21 10–12 PDT or Wed 9/22 13–15 PDT. Either works.

—
Alex Cho

Alex — looping in a couple of technical points so the workshop can be scoped correctly. Short, practical notes: 

1) Migration of quantized checkpoints (from your on-prem):
- We support importing 8-bit/4-bit quantized checkpoints. The main work is standardizing the tokenizer and ensuring the KV cache layout matches the runtime (we can convert KV snapshots as part of the migration tool). Expect ~3–5 days of hands-on engineering per model for validation and acceptance tests (less if you have CI).

2) KV cache and warmup strategies:
- For chat routes with strict p95 targets, we recommend a prefix-KV warmup during seasonal spikes and a small dedicated warm pool on Dedicated or Private to keep cold-starts below 50ms. We can also ship a pre-warmed snapshot for your legacy state.

3) Networking + VPC peering (short checklist):
- VPC peering or PrivateLink (customer preference)
- Allow outbound TLS (443) to our control plane for metrics/rollouts; we can also run a fully air-gapped control plane in Private installs.
- Port list for data plane: 443 (TLS), 10250 (control agent), and optional metrics ports we can tunnel. We'll provide an exact port table in the security packet.

4) SLA / throughput notes for Dedicated vs Private:
- Dedicated: predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools; autoscale policies for spikes but limited burst headroom (can add burst credits).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): you own the capacity and we surface the same runtime; SLA alignment depends on your infra and SRE agreement.

I’ll prepare a short migration plan template we can fill during the workshop (model list, KV migration steps, acceptance tests, rollback plan).

Next step: Karthik — can you lock Wed 9/22 13:00–15:00 PDT and include SRE and security contacts from FinPay?

Cheers,
